response.title: A Garden Shared by Two Clubs
response.passage:
The science club planned a small vegetable garden beside the library. Since each member brought a different skill, the students agreed to cooperate rather than leave all the work to one person. Mina measured the space, while Leo checked which vegetables could grow in shade. After comparing Mina’s measurements with Leo’s list of shade-tolerant vegetables, the club chose to reserve one corner for herbs the cooking club might need later. To place the remaining boxes well, the students decided to observe how sunlight reached the area at different times of day. Their observations showed that the wall blocked afternoon sun, so they moved the boxes to a brighter spot.

In early May, a shortage of clean pots threatened the planting schedule. The club counted its supplies and found only six usable pots, although ten seedlings were ready. The students asked the art class for help, and together they cleaned old paint containers for reuse. The recycled containers gave each seedling a safe place to grow without delaying the project. By the end of the month, the garden was growing well, and both clubs were proud of their shared work.
